items.title: What does an abstraction need to preserve?
items.status: Owner-local research candidate; finite synthetic tests
items.summary: The Lab is testing whether abstractions can be understood relative to the questions and continuations they must support. Exact quotient and transition-congruence criteria are established mathematics; an internal finite verifier exercised those cases.
items.limitation: The broader epistemic-factorization thesis remains a hypothesis. Internal synthetic checks do not establish novelty, universal adequacy or independent external validation.

items.title: A proposed machine for testing representations
items.summary: The Boundary Executor design describes an interface for bounded checks of state, admissibility, preserved consequences, evidence, and repair obligations.
items.limitation: This proposed general machine is not a registered or validated Lab Machine; existing narrow instruments do not establish a universal executor.

items.title: Comparing the assumptions beneath mathematical foundations
items.summary: A new research capture frames comparisons among existing mathematical foundational systems and the proposed bound-distinction construction.
items.limitation: This is a comparison program, not a theorem replacing set theory or establishing a more fundamental mathematics.
